symptom: `make test` reports `FAIL github.com/mendixlabs/mxcli/mdl/linter` with `panic: test timed out after 10m0s` in a PR that never touched the package; the package passes when run on its own, and whether it trips depends on the machine
cause: `make test` ran `go test ./...` with no `-timeout`, so each test binary got Go's 10m default. Under `./...` every package runs at once and a package's wall time is set by machine load: mdl/linter takes ~25s alone (most of it pure-Go SQLite catalog fixtures, ~0.3s each) and was measured at 552s and 872s inside `make test`
insight: Time the reported package ALONE first (`go test -count=1 -json ./pkg` and sort by Elapsed): 25s against a reported 552-872s means contention, not a slow test, so optimising the test is the wrong turn and the fix is the limit. `-timeout` is per test binary and counts wall time, so it cannot tell a slow package from a starved one, and Go's default is a limit nobody chose. Reproduce the exact symptom cheaply with a tiny limit (`go test -timeout 5s ./mdl/linter` -> `panic: test timed out after 5s`) to show the flag is the knob. Fresh-checkout aside: run `make sync-all` before timing mdl/linter, or TestCONV006/TestSEC008 fail on missing `cmd/mxcli/lint-rules/*.star` and look like the bug
